summary: CPU scheduling decides which process in the ready queue gets the CPU next. FCFS (First Come First Serve) runs the first-arriving process first; it is non-preemptive and simple, but can cause the convoy effect where short processes wait behind a long one. SJF (Shortest Job First) runs the process with the smallest burst time first, offering the minimum average waiting time, though it requires knowing burst times in advance and can cause starvation for long processes. Round Robin (RR) gives each process a fixed time quantum before moving it to the back of the ready queue, making it preemptive and good for time-sharing systems, though a quantum that is too large makes it act like FCFS and one that is too small causes excessive context switches. Finally, waiting time is calculated as turnaround time minus burst time, and turnaround time is completion time minus arrival time.
